memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'"yet because of his defect, he must not go near the curtain or
approach the altar, and so desecrate my sanctuary. I am the LORD, who
makes them holy"'" - Lev 21:23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The curtain appears again. That thick veil separating the Most Holy
Place stood as a constant reminder: God is holy, and sinful people
cannot simply walk in. Every restriction in this chapter served that
one message.

For centuries the curtain hung there. Then, on the day Jesus died,
Matthew records that the curtain of the temple was torn in two from
top to bottom (Matt 27:51). Top to bottom - torn from God's side, not
ours. No human hand did that.

Hebrews explains what it meant. We now have confidence to enter the
Most Holy Place by the blood of Jesus, by a new and living way opened
for us through the curtain, that is, His body (Heb 10:19-20).

Dear friend, sit with that for a moment. Everything Leviticus 21 kept
at a distance, Christ has brought near. Not by lowering God's holiness,
but by satisfying it completely.

And notice the last phrase once more: "I am the LORD, who makes them
holy." Four times in this chapter God says holiness is His work. It
was true then. It is gloriously true now.

You do not approach God because you have qualified. You approach
because Christ has qualified you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I truly believe I can come to God with confidence through Christ?
2. What still makes me hesitate to draw near to Him?
3. How can I thank God today for the torn curtain?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that the curtain is torn and the way is open. Give
me confidence to draw near through Jesus, and never let me take that
open door for granted. Amen.
